newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israel hits Lebanon on eve of donors conference.
newsitem.headline: Israel hits Lebanon on eve of donors conference.

text.p: Israeli planes rocketed suspected guerrilla targets in Lebanon three times on Sunday amid a flare-up of violence on the eve of a U.S.-sponsored donors conference for the Middle Eastern country.

The planes fired a dozen rockets into remote south-eastern hills used by pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas to launch attacks on troops garrisoning Israel's occupation zone along the Lebanese border.

The raids followed a clash in the zone on Saturday in which Israel said an Israeli brigadier was slightly hurt and two Moslem guerrillas were killed. On Friday, Israel said Katyusha rockets fired from Lebanon hit northern Israel.

Beirut newspapers commented gloomily that the weekend violence on the last active Arab-Israeli battlefront would do Lebanon's image no good in the eyes of potential donors at Monday's "Friends of Lebanon" conference in Washington.

Billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, who is heading Lebanon's delegation to the conference, will ask some 30 nations to contribute up to $5 billion for reconstruction projects over the next five years.

The U.S. State Department has promised important announcements at the conference and Lebanese officials hope that means Washington will ease its 11-year-old ban on U.S. citizens travelling to Beirut and air links between the two countries.

The officials say Lebanon deserves political support and financial help after making a huge effort in the past four years to rebuild and to restore economic, political, social and security stability after the 1975-90 civil war.
But Sunday's air raids symbolised the continuing threat of instability that Lebanon faces while Israeli troops hold part of its territory and Moslem guerrillas continue to attack them.
As the Israeli planes struck columns of smoke rose from the rocky hillsides of southeast Lebanon but a Hizbollah spokesman in Beirut told Reuters he had no immediate word of casualties.

The planes twice hit the eastern side of the central Lebanese mountains overlooking the Bekaa valley, firing eight rockets into the hills between the towns of Mashgara and Ain el-Tineh, security sources said.
Five minutes later they fired four more rockets into the Jabbour hills seven km (four miles) further south, near the edge of the Israeli occupation zone, the sources added.
Two aircraft carried out each strike while four others circled overhead.

On Saturday, Israel complained to a five-nation monitoring group that Katyusha rockets which it said were fired at northern Israel on Friday violated a U.S.-sponsored ceasefire understanding banning attacks on civilian areas on both sides of the Lebanese-Israeli border. Hizbollah denied firing rockets.

The monitoring group was formed to supervise the April 26 ceasefire understanding which ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon intended to destroy Hizbollah. The group comprises the United States, France, Syria, Lebanon and Israel.

In three rulings it has issued on the basis of Lebanese complaints since starting work in October, it has held Israel responsible for breaching the ceasefire understanding by bombarding civilian areas in south Lebanon and injuring civilians. It has twice said it "deplores" Israeli actions.
